# Load initial data

This is the primary data set and includes Box Scores for each player in each game

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
players <- read_csv("./data/PlayerStatistics.csv")
```

# Find how many teams don't exist anymore

```{r}
players %>% 
  filter(year(gameDate) > 1970) %>% 
  distinct(playerteamCity) %>% 
  anti_join(
    players %>% 
      filter(year(gameDate) == 2024) %>% 
      distinct(playerteamCity),
    by = "playerteamCity"
  )
```

# Blean Box Scores

Filter data to certain date (2015) and remove international teams

```{r}
players <- players %>%
  filter(year(gameDate)>=2015,
         gameType %in% c("Playoffs", "Regular Season", "Play-in Tournament", NA),
         numMinutes>0,
         !playerteamName %in% c("United", "Loong-Lions", "Jerusalem B.C.", "Pheonix"))
```

# Load Secondary dataset

each row in this dataset is a unique game/team used for calculating win rates and thats it

```{r}
library(lubridate)
Team_Data <- read_csv("data/TeamStatistics.csv")

Team_Data <- Team_Data %>% 
  select( gameDate, teamName, teamId, opponentTeamName, opponentTeamId, gameId, home, win, teamScore, assists, teamCity, steals, fieldGoalsAttempted, fieldGoalsMade, fieldGoalsPercentage, threePointersPercentage, freeThrowsPercentage, reboundsTotal, pointsFastBreak, pointsFromTurnovers, pointsSecondChance, pointsInThePaint) %>% 
  # clean data 
  # There were some international teams that were removed
  #filter(!(teamId %in% c(15016,15018, 50013, 50014))) %>% 
  filter(year(gameDate) >= 2015)

Team_Data %>% distinct(teamName)
```

# Calculate win rate

Basically, its pretty hard to quantifiable say what contributes to a team culture and measure it quantitatively. One of the ways this can be measured is through win rate.

```{r}
#Calculating win rate for every team

win_rate_data <- Team_Data %>%
  group_by(teamName) %>% 
  summarise(total_wins = sum(win), total_games = n()) %>%
  mutate(winRate= total_wins / total_games) 

win_rate_data %>% 
  select(teamName, winRate) %>% 
  arrange(desc(winRate))
```

In order to visualize the win rate and which teams are good and bad we created a column diagram with ggplot. The graph was flipped on its side and a line at 0.5 win rate was introduced, to show the cut of for a good/bad team. Teams with a win rate over 50% was given a green color and teams with a win rate below 50% was given a red color.

```{r}
win_rate_data %>% 
  mutate(color_group = ifelse(winRate < 0.5, "red", "green")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(teamName, winRate), 
             y = winRate,
             fill = color_group)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed")+      # line at 0.5
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0.35, 0.65)) +                      # zoomed graph around line at 0.5
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red" = "#F44336",       
                               "green" = "#4CAF50"))+    # assinging color
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + 
  guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(y = "Win Rate", x = "Team")

```

# Bulk Calculation of career averages

career caluclates each players average standard deviations for their major stats zScores for each game and given their career mean and standard dev. then by team, calculates each players average z score for each stat on that team in their career

So for example, players who played on one team their whole career would have a zAvgPPG and zAvgPPM of 0. However, if a player played for the Lakers and Cavaliers but had higher PPG stats on the cavaliers then the their entries would look like the following:

```{r}
#LeBron
byTeam %>% 
  filter(personId == 2544) %>% 
  select(playerteamName, year, zAvgPPG)
```

Positive values are better than average performances and negative are worse than average

```{r}
career <- players %>% 
  group_by(personId) %>% 
  mutate(PPM = points/numMinutes) %>% 
  summarize(careerPPM = mean(PPM),
            careerPPG = mean(points),
            careerGames = n(),
            careerMinutes = sum(numMinutes),
            sdPoints = sd(points),
            sdPPM = sd(PPM),
            careerFAPG = mean(fieldGoalsAttempted),
            sdFAPG = sd(fieldGoalsAttempted),
            careerFGP = mean(fieldGoalsPercentage),
            sdFGP = sd(fieldGoalsPercentage)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(sdPoints))

zPlayers <- players %>% 
  inner_join(career, by = join_by(personId == personId)) %>% 
  mutate(PPM = points/numMinutes,
         zPPG = (points-careerPPG)/sdPoints,
         zPPM = (PPM-careerPPM)/sdPPM,
         zFAPG = (fieldGoalsAttempted-careerFAPG)/sdFAPG,
         zFGP = (fieldGoalsPercentage-careerFGP)/sdFGP)

byTeam <- zPlayers %>% 
  filter(numMinutes>0) %>%
  mutate(year = year(gameDate)) %>% 
  group_by(personId, playerteamName, year) %>% 
  mutate(PPM = points/numMinutes) %>% 
  summarize(teamPPM = mean(PPM),
            teamPPG = mean(points),
            teamGames = n(),
            teamMinutes = sum(numMinutes),
            zAvgPPG = mean(zPPG),
            zAvgPPM = mean(zPPM),
            zAvgFAPG = mean(zFAPG),
            zAvgFGP = mean(zFGP))

#names <- players %>% select(firstName, lastName, personId)

#names %>% filter(lastName == "Westbrook")

# not sure why I can't do the below instead of the above filter. Somehow this causes byTeam to ungroup

  # left_join(names, by = "personId") %>% 
  # relocate(firstName, lastName, zAvgPPG, zAvgPPM,playerteamName, .before = 1) %>% 
  # filter(firstName == "LeBron")

#There are a couple of people for whom have played<3 games and scored <2 points that cause avgZssoc to be NA
#See below code chunk
```

#Calculate Team Association indexes by year Now, we average the zAvgPPG for each player who played for said team since 2015, weighted by the minutes a player played for that team. We weight it because the results starter who player \>70 games a season matter more than a bench player who played in \<10 games a season.

```{r}
teamAssoc <- byTeam %>% 
  group_by(playerteamName, year) %>% 
  summarize(avgAssocPPG = mean(zAvgPPG*teamMinutes, na.rm = TRUE),
            avgAssocPPM = mean(zAvgPPM*teamMinutes, na.rm = TRUE),
            avgAssocFAPG = mean(zAvgFAPG*teamMinutes, na.rm = TRUE),
            avgAssocFGP = mean(zAvgFGP*teamMinutes, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avgAssocPPG))

teamAssoc %>% arrange()
```

#Finding data for total teams & corelation between indexes

We explored if any of the indexes seem to have a correlation between each other. They do. attempts, PPG and PPM all have a positive correlation. But FGP does not

```{r}

totalTeamAssoc <- teamAssoc %>% 
  group_by(playerteamName) %>% 
  select(-year) %>% 
  summarize_all(mean) %>% 
  left_join(win_rate_data, join_by(playerteamName == teamName))
totalTeamAssoc

totalTeamAssoc %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = avgAssocFAPG, y = avgAssocPPG)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
print("correlation between attempts and PPG")
cor.test(totalTeamAssoc$avgAssocFAPG, totalTeamAssoc$avgAssocPPG)

totalTeamAssoc %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = avgAssocFAPG, y = avgAssocPPM)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
print("correlation between attempts and PPM")
cor.test(totalTeamAssoc$avgAssocFAPG, totalTeamAssoc$avgAssocPPM)

print("correlation between attempts and FGP")
totalTeamAssoc %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = avgAssocFAPG, y = avgAssocFGP)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
cor.test(totalTeamAssoc$avgAssocFAPG, totalTeamAssoc$avgAssocFGP)
```

# Testing win rate vs indexes

testing a correlation between win rate and the indexes of teams There seems to exist a probable correlation

```{r}
totalTeamAssoc %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = winRate, y = avgAssocPPG)) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm")
cor.test(totalTeamAssoc$winRate, totalTeamAssoc$avgAssocPPG)

totalTeamAssoc %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = winRate, y = avgAssocFGP)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
cor.test(totalTeamAssoc$winRate, totalTeamAssoc$avgAssocPPG)
```

# Testing the indexes in ANOVA

anova testing only shows signifcance of a relationship between PPG and teams This partially contradicts correlation testing

```{r}
teamAssocB <- teamAssoc %>% 
  left_join(win_rate_data, join_by(playerteamName == teamName))

modelPPG <- aov(avgAssocPPG ~ playerteamName, data = teamAssocB)
summary(modelPPG)

modelFGP <- aov(avgAssocFGP ~ poly(winRate,2), data = teamAssocB)
summary(modelFGP)
```

# Graphing the indexes for last 10 years by team

summarize the major index values: PPG and FGP FGAP and PPM correlate already with PPG so not graphed

```{r}
library(ggthemes)

totalTeamAssoc %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(playerteamName, avgZssocPPG), 
             y = avgZssocPPG, 
             fill = avgZssocPPG > 0)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Average Player Over/Underperformance by Franchise",
       subtitle = "Measured in effect index relative to each player’s own career average",
       x = "Franchise",
       y = "Weighted Avg effect index (Points per Game)") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#4CAF50", "FALSE" = "#F44336")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

totalTeamAssoc %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(playerteamName, avgZssocFGP), 
             y = avgZssocFGP, 
             fill = avgZssocFGP > 0)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Average Player Over/Underperformance by Franchise",
       subtitle = "Measured in effect index relative to each player’s own career average",
       x = "Franchise",
       y = "Weighted Avg effect index (Field Goal Percentage)") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#4CAF50", "FALSE" = "#F44336")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

# What do indexes mean?

So far the indexes have been abstract. Here is a sample table that shows how much of an effect our indexes mean. Its very small. We estimate that the strongest effect is \~2 extra PPG or \~2% more FG%

```{r}
yearTested <- 2025

mins <- byTeam %>%
  filter(year == yearTested) %>% 
  group_by(playerteamName) %>% 
  summarize(avgTeamMinutes = mean(teamMinutes))

weightedSds <- career %>% 
  filter(careerMinutes!=0) %>% 
  summarize(centralSdFgp = mean(sdFGP*careerMinutes),
            meanCareerMinutes = mean(careerMinutes),
            centralSdPpg = mean(sdPoints*careerMinutes)) %>% 
  mutate(SdFgp = centralSdFgp/meanCareerMinutes,
         SdPpg = centralSdPpg/meanCareerMinutes)
  
left_join(totalTeamAssoc, mins, by = "playerteamName") %>% 
  mutate(FgpEffect = avgAssocFGP*weightedSds$SdFgp/avgTeamMinutes*100,
         PpgEffect = avgAssocPPG*weightedSds$SdPpg/avgTeamMinutes) %>% 
  arrange(desc(PpgEffect)) %>% 
  relocate(PpgEffect, FgpEffect, avgAssocPPG, avgAssocFGP, .after = 1) 

rm(mins,weightedSds)
```
